title: General Cooktop Fault
shortDescription: The cooktop has detected an unspecified internal fault.
fullDescription: A solitary 'F' on the display is AEG's generic fault indicator. It is most often a transient event cleared by a power-cycle; persistent F indicates an inverter or control-board problem.

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cut the breaker for 10 minutes then restore.

fixSteps.title: Call service
fixSteps.instruction: If F persists, a technician must test the inverter.

faq.a: Yes — storms commonly trigger generic faults.

title: Coil Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: An induction coil sensor is out of range.
fullDescription: Error F2 indicates the NTC sensor under a coil is open or shorted. The affected zone is disabled until repair.

fixSteps.title: Cut power
fixSteps.instruction: Shut the breaker and wait 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Call service
fixSteps.instruction: Glass and coil removal are required — engage a technician.

videoSearchQuery: AEG cooktop F2 sensor error fix

faq.q: Can I use the other zones?
faq.a: Yes, only the affected zone is disabled.

title: Cooling Fan Fault
shortDescription: The electronics cooling fan has failed.
fullDescription: Error F4 indicates the fan that cools the inverter is not spinning or is drawing abnormal current. The cooktop throttles power and eventually shuts down to avoid electronics overheat.

fixSteps.title: Clear the cabinet
fixSteps.instruction: Remove items obstructing airflow under the cooktop.

videoSearchQuery: AEG cooktop F4 fan error fix

faq.a: Yes, flour and lint clog the intake over time.

title: Touch Control Fault
shortDescription: The touch control panel is unresponsive or reports a stuck key.
fullDescription: Error F6 indicates the glass touch sensors are reporting a key pressed for too long. Water, debris, or a cracked touch area are the usual causes.

fixSteps.title: Clean the glass
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe dry and remove any metal object from above the touch pad.

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cut the breaker for five minutes.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning fails, the touch module must be replaced by a technician.
videoSearchQuery: AEG cooktop F6 touch error fix

faq.a: Yes — never lay towels over the touch area while cooking.

title: Inverter Module Fault
shortDescription: An inverter power module has failed.
fullDescription: Error F8 indicates an IGBT or related power component in the inverter has failed. Typically one side of the cooktop loses power.

fixSteps.title: Cut power
fixSteps.instruction: Shut the breaker and stop using the cooktop.

videoSearchQuery: AEG cooktop F8 inverter error fix

faq.a: Often yes in the first two years — check paperwork.

title: Coil Overheat Warning
shortDescription: An induction zone has reached its thermal limit.
fullDescription: Error E1 is shown when a coil's temperature sensor reads too high. The zone disables until the coil cools. Empty pots or warped bases are typical triggers.

fixSteps.title: Remove the pan
fixSteps.instruction: Lift cookware and let the zone cool for 10-15 minutes.

whenToCallPro: Only if E1 persists cold — possible sensor fault.
videoSearchQuery: AEG cooktop E1 overheat error fix

faq.a: Yes, uneven contact concentrates heat in one spot.

title: Unsuitable Cookware
shortDescription: The cooktop does not detect ferromagnetic cookware on the zone.
fullDescription: Error E2 (sometimes shown as 'U') indicates the pan on the zone is not induction-compatible, is too small, or has a warped base preventing coupling with the coil.

fixSteps.title: Magnet test
fixSteps.instruction: A kitchen magnet must stick firmly to the pan base.

fixSteps.title: Match zone size
fixSteps.instruction: Use a pan equal to or larger than the marked diameter.

videoSearchQuery: AEG cooktop E2 cookware error fix

faq.a: Yes — cast iron works well on induction.

title: Electronics Overheat
shortDescription: The inverter compartment is too hot.
fullDescription: Error E3 indicates the temperature of the electronics compartment is too high. The cooktop throttles or shuts down zones until the inverter cools.

fixSteps.title: Improve ventilation
fixSteps.instruction: Clear the cabinet below the cooktop.

whenToCallPro: If E3 recurs with a clear cabinet, call service to inspect the fan.
videoSearchQuery: AEG cooktop E3 overheat error fix

faq.a: Yes. The minimum airflow gaps prevent E3.

title: Voltage Out Of Range
shortDescription: Mains voltage is outside the safe operating range.
fullDescription: Error E4 indicates the cooktop measured mains voltage too high or too low. The cooktop disables heating to prevent inverter damage.

fixSteps.title: Observe other appliances
fixSteps.instruction: If lights flicker, call the utility.

fixSteps.title: Call an electrician
fixSteps.instruction: Have the terminal block and branch circuit inspected.

videoSearchQuery: AEG cooktop E4 voltage error fix

faq.a: Yes. Stop using it until the wiring is confirmed good.

title: Mains Frequency Out Of Range
shortDescription: The mains frequency has drifted outside the safe range.
fullDescription: Error E5 indicates the cooktop has detected mains frequency out of spec. This is uncommon on stable grids and can indicate a generator supply, severe utility problem, or control-board sensing fault.

fixSteps.title: Confirm power source
fixSteps.instruction: If running on a generator, verify it supports sensitive electronics.

fixSteps.title: Call service
fixSteps.instruction: If on utility and E5 persists, the control board may be at fault.

whenToCallPro: Whenever E5 recurs on utility power.
videoSearchQuery: AEG cooktop E5 frequency error fix

faq.a: No — induction cooktops need a pure-sine inverter generator sized above 6 kW.
